comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch full-time 2026–2027 VU bachelor (RIO56003) is taught in the ACASA VU–UvA collaboration on the UvA campus. There are no formal specialisations. The adopted OER Articles11.1–11.4 establish ten compulsory6EC first-year units, thirteen compulsory6EC later units, a12EC thesis including colloquium and30EC genuine open study:180EC. The standard programme is used, not the shortened UvA-entry pathway or pre2017 transition. Comedy is an optional additional6EC module, as the visible Appendix4 footnote confirms, despite appearing unqualified on recruitment pages; it is not added to the compulsory total. Article9.1 requires a positive BSA for post-first-year assessment, subject to catalogue conditions; thesis entry requires all first- and second-year courses. Article14.1 normally requires48first-yearEC for a positive full-time BSA. Article10.4 requires a Dutch diagnostic test and, on failure, the remedial course, outside180EC. Article11.5 requires85% attendance for Historical Sources, Philosophy of the Humanities, ACASA Excursion and Reception/Creative Writing, otherwise repeat or an additional assignment. Article12.1 allows a minor, electives, study abroad or up to12EC internship; outside VU/UvA needs examination-board approval. Normally at most12EC introductory study, exceptionally24EC for specified VU/UvA minors or one-language acquisition packages; foreign language-improvement courses outside an academic degree do not qualify. Minor course prerequisites still apply. Optional honours are additional, not part of180EC. Thesis is disciplinary research; Article3.10 guarantees draft feedback under the thesis regulation. Programme tutoring occurs at least twice per year (Article7.3).

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The current workbook supports comparative reading across Greek, Roman and other mythic traditions, including Ovid, close reading and stylistics, Greek and Roman rhetorical theory, Athenian material and textual evidence, and modern reception and creative methods. The strongest feasible 24-course assembly extends these methods across literature, art and philosophy. Its research seminar addresses American history. None of the available courses supports a progression of original-language Greek and Latin reading and translation, historical grammar, and sustained research on classical texts.

candidateAssessment.label: Classical literature, rhetoric and cultural reception
candidateAssessment.reason: Comparative mythology, rhetorical analysis, stylistics, adaptation and creative writing support genuine related inquiry. Ancient epic is taught within comparative literature, while advanced creative and critical work uses broad materials. The assembly cannot sustain original-text philology or research on Greek and Latin texts across periods.

candidateAssessment.label: Ancient Mediterranean history and public memory
candidateAssessment.reason: Greek Archaeology, Heritage & Ancient Democracy and comparative empires support a strong Athenian case and wider material context. Art history and museums provide broader reception and memory methods. This direction lacks the target sequence in Greek and Latin historiography, genres, linguistics and text-based independent research.

candidateAssessment.label: Classical reception and creative rewriting
candidateAssessment.reason: The strongest attempt already combines mythic transmission, literary adaptation and creative work. The workbook does not support an additional sequence centred on the reception of original Greek and Latin texts.

candidateAssessment.label: Teaching Greek and Latin
candidateAssessment.reason: Teaching is a conditional minor or later qualification in the VU programme. Related UCR public-speaking practice does not sustain subject-specific Greek and Latin teaching or the classical text work that would underpin it.

audience.programmeDescription: The joint VU–UvA programme develops close reading and interpretation of Greek and Latin texts through language study, linguistics, literature, ancient history and philosophy. Students also examine how later societies interpreted antiquity and complete an independent classics thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial related study in Greek archaeology, Athenian democracy, rhetoric and comparative mythology, including Ovid. VU builds from reading and translating Greek and Latin to interpreting original texts, studying how both languages changed, and conducting independent classics research. UCR’s related courses do not form that sustained sequence in classical texts and languages.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC curriculum includes 30 EC of elective study and a 12 EC thesis with a colloquium. Comedy is optional. The Dutch language test and any required remedial course carry no credits. Four specified courses require at least 85% attendance.
